findings.title: Missing-design fallback can silently assign the wrong biological groups
evidence: transcriptomics_architecture_runbook.md:33,82,85 require ID validation but omit the missing-design branch
transcriptomics_workflow.rmd:126-137 assigns the first six sample columns to RPMI and the next six to Sera, without sample metadata
findings.impact: A reordered 12-sample input can have unique, matching IDs while the treatment labels are wrong. Preserving the notebook algorithm is not sufficient scientific authority for that branch.
findings.repair: Explicitly map the design-file fallback. Require authoritative sample-to-group metadata for general use; retain the automatic labels only for an explicitly bound workshop fixture. Treat changing fallback behavior as an agreed correctness decision, separate from performance parity.
findings.closure_evidence: Runbook names the branch and decision. Before implementation acceptance, test reordered sample columns and missing design: no silent reassignment; supplied authoritative labels remain attached to their Run IDs.

findings.title: Disk ingress lacks a concrete producer-to-codec mapping
evidence: transcriptomics_architecture_runbook.md:33,71-74,94 prescribe disk ingress and staged writing
transcriptomics_workflow.rmd:121 reads the original text table through vroom
R/utils_workflow_saved_table_codec.R:542-555 newWorkflowTableReadScope requires an existing Parquet descriptor
R/utils_workflow_saved_table_codec.R:130 writeSavedWorkflowParquet takes an already materialized table
findings.impact: The first text-to-owned-table boundary is not identified as missing adaptation work. Following the named read/write helpers alone can retain the original ingestion memory spike.
findings.repair: Name an explicit proposed text-ingestion adapter boundary, distinguish it from existing helpers, and specify bounded parsing or scoped engine ingestion into the existing staged codec with schema, original row ordinal, parse-failure and ownership requirements. Do not claim that an importer has already been qualified.
findings.closure_evidence: The map traces source text to staged encoded table to accepted reference without assuming a pre-existing reference. Future implementation proof covers bounded parsing, duplicate keys, type errors and cleanup after partial ingestion.

findings.title: Gene-scale annotations and masks have no route above the lookup ceiling
evidence: transcriptomics_architecture_runbook.md:18,34,44,74 map masks/lookups and bulk lookup loading without a large-lookup alternative
R/utils_workflow_saved_table_codec.R:3088-3093 workflowQueryWriteLookup refuses native tables above 10000 rows
Read-only R probe with 10001 GeneID rows returned saved_entity_limit: invalid native lookup table
findings.impact: Larger gene annotation or feature-mask tables cannot use the suggested small-lookup path. Repeated calls with the same name also recreate the table rather than append it.
findings.repair: State the exact lookup row/byte ceilings and route larger masks/annotations through saved tables and scoped joins. Identify any necessary binding adaptation; do not raise the ceiling or repeatedly invoke CREATE TABLE as an implicit workaround.
findings.closure_evidence: Map includes below/at/above-limit cases and a separate durable-table route; future tests prove 10000/10001 rows, join cardinality, exact keys/order and no full-result collection.

findings.title: Existing wide-table streaming helper is omitted
evidence: transcriptomics_architecture_runbook.md:14,72 discusses the 64-column primitive and asks for column-stripe assembly
R/utils_workflow_saved_table_codec.R:2144-2165 streamWorkflowTableRows already reads wide tables in <=64-column blocks, assembles <=10000-row batches and checks a 64 MiB batch ceiling
findings.impact: The instructions can lead to duplicating existing infrastructure and miss its whole-wide-batch byte limitation. Very wide sample-by-gene integration exports need byte-based admission even when row counts are small.
findings.repair: Map streamWorkflowTableRows as the first existing reuse candidate for wide outputs and matrix input assembly. Keep qualification of row identity and byte limits explicit. Separate this helper from the lower-level streamSavedWorkflowTable limit and mark very-wide overflow as a bounded adaptation decision.
findings.closure_evidence: Updated map names helper, existing consumers and limits; future focused checks cover 64/65 columns, complete row identity and the combined wide-batch byte ceiling.

findings.title: Early optimization sequence lacks the required profiling gate
evidence: transcriptomics_architecture_runbook.md:93-97 stages ingress, ownership and RLE changes; explicit profiling appears only before the final alternative-kernel step
AGENTS.md requires an identified measured cost before optimization
conventions/R.md Performance requires profiling before optimizing
findings.impact: The candidate map is reasonable, but implementing stages 2-4 in the stated order without attribution can add persistence, scans or exact-quantile state without a meaningful memory benefit.
findings.repair: Keep this as a candidate map and add a small non-GUI baseline/attribution gate before choosing any performance adaptation. Select one mechanism from measured cost, then compare complete operations. Include import copies, simultaneous matrices, RLE long-table retention and quantile working state; do not authorize a new benchmark campaign in the runbook.
findings.closure_evidence: Sequence explicitly requires baseline attribution before candidate selection; future bounded comparison freezes input/build, memory-first criterion and allowed runtime tradeoff before outcomes.
